The cancelled word preserves the tall initial f, the raised middle t and the low terminal hooked group. The same page’s clear facteur has the corresponding f–t spacing, although cancellation conceals most small counters here.

The raised insertion has a long downstroke ending in a small shoulder, then a dot and detached terminal bar. Its o/m/b bodies cannot be separated securely from the horizontal ink above, so the full word versus a contraction remains unsettled.

Despite the strike-through, the initial o/n loop, the a loop and dotted i of sait, its tall crossed t, and the long q descender of que remain in sequence.

The deleted phrase retains the low de group, the tall t and lower return in type, an isolated upright I with a foot, and the tall p followed by a low ur connection. Several cancellation strokes cross the small bodies but leave those spaced components visible.
